articles.title: Indígenas viajam mais de 7h de barco por rio no Pantanal para votar | G1
articles.standfirst: Quatro embarcações fizeram o trajeto, e uma delas precisou de reparos após furar. Segundo o cacique, pelo menos 34 moradores não conseguiram sair da aldeia para votar.
articles.summary: Quatro embarcações fizeram o trajeto, e uma delas precisou de reparos após furar. Segundo o cacique, pelo menos 34 moradores não conseguiram sair da aldeia para votar.
articles.body:
Indígenas da aldeia Barra do São Lourenço e brigadistas que atuam no combate a incêndios em áreas remotas do Pantanal viajaram por mais de sete horas de barco pelo rio Paraguai para votar neste domingo (25), em Corumbá , no oeste de Mato Grosso do Sul. As primeiras embarcações chegaram ao Porto Geral por volta das 12h35, após saírem da comunidade às 5h. Veja o vídeo acima.

Ao todo, quatro embarcações fizeram o trajeto para transportar os moradores até a área urbana do município. Durante a viagem, uma delas furou e precisou passar por reparos, o que atrasou o deslocamento. A aldeia Barra do São Lourenço fica a cerca de 260 quilômetros da área urbana de Corumbá.

A chegada das primeiras embarcações ocorreu ao longo do período da manhã e início da tarde. Os moradores precisaram percorrer o trecho fluvial para chegar a Corumbá e participar da votação do segundo turno das eleições.

Parte dos moradores fez a viagem em embarcações da própria comunidade. Outros conseguiram carona com a Brigada do Instituto Homem Pantaneiro (IHP), que auxiliou no transporte dos eleitores.

Segundo o cacique Negré, da aldeia da Barra do São Lourenço, pelo menos 34 pessoas não conseguiram deixar a aldeia para votar neste domingo. O cacique afirmou que os moradores organizaram a viagem até Corumbá com a ajuda de pessoas da região, após não receberem o apoio logístico que esperavam do Exército e da Fundação Nacional dos Povos Indígenas (Funai).

“Para nós, é muito importante exercer a nossa cidadania, porque aí nós podemos escolher a pessoa que queremos para governar o nosso país, o nosso estado. Nós queremos também ter esse direito de escolher”, disse.

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Corumbá informou à Defensoria Pública da União que não tem estrutura para transportar os eleitores indígenas das aldeias Uberaba e Barra do São Lourenço no segundo turno. O Exército afirmou que não recebeu pedido de apoio e que não está autorizado a transportar eleitores em embarcações ou viaturas militares. Já a Marinha informou que o apoio às eleições é organizado com a Justiça Eleitoral e que pedidos adicionais devem ser encaminhados ao Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Mato Grosso do Sul (TRE-MS).

Leia na íntegra o que a Prefeitura de Corumbá disse:

"Em resposta à solicitação de transporte para os indígenas Guató das aldeias Uberaba e Barra do São Lourenço, no Pantanal de Corumbá, a Prefeitura de Corumbá informou à Defensoria Pública da União que não tem condições operacionais de garantir o deslocamento dos eleitores no segundo turno das eleições. Em ofício datado de 21 de outubro de 2026 e encaminhado à Defensoria Pública da União, em Campo Grande, o Município esclareceu que não dispõe de embarcações ou veículos adequados, com capacidade, tripulação e condições de segurança necessárias para realizar o transporte de ida e volta. A administração também informou que não mantém um serviço regular de transporte para essas comunidades. No documento, a Prefeitura defendeu uma articulação urgente entre a Justiça Eleitoral, a Funai, órgãos federais e o Governo do Estado para buscar alternativas. O Município pode contribuir com informações e apoio administrativo, mas não tem estrutura para assegurar o deslocamento dos eleitores".

"Em relação ao transporte de eleitores da comunidade de Forte Coimbra, em Corumbá (MS), o Comando Operacional Conjunto Oeste esclarece que o apoio às Eleições 2026 está sendo organizado em conjunto com a Justiça Eleitoral, conforme as solicitações recebidas do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) e autorizadas pelo Ministério da Defesa (MD). Qualquer apoio além do já previsto pelo TSE deve ser encaminhado ao TRE-MS".

"1. O Comando da 18ª Brigada de Infantaria de Pantanal não recebeu solicitação dessa natureza. 2. De acordo com a legislação vigente, o Exército não está autorizado a transportar eleitores em viaturas ou embarcações militares. 3. No tocante ao Comando da 18ª Brigada de Infantaria de Pantanal, não há articulações nesse sentido. 4. ⁠Não houve solicitações, até o momento, dessa natureza".

articles.title: Jiboia em local de votação: cobra é capturada em escola de Itaúna | G1
articles.standfirst: Serpente foi encontrada presa à grade de uma sala na manhã deste domingo (25), na comunidade Retiro dos Farias, em Itaúna, no Centro-Oeste do estado. O animal foi solto em habitat natural.
articles.summary: Bombeiros capturaram uma jiboia presa à grade de uma escola usada como local de votação em Itaúna, Minas Gerais, na manhã deste domingo.
articles.body:
Cobra é capturada em local de votação em Itaúna — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Divulgação

Uma jiboia foi capturada na manhã deste domingo (25) em uma escola que funciona como local de votação da 140ª Zona Eleitoral, na comunidade de Retiro dos Farias, em Itaúna , no Centro-Oeste de Minas Gerais.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, a equipe foi acionada às 7h43, após a serpente ser encontrada presa à grade da porta de uma sala na área externa.

A jiboia foi capturada seguindo os procedimentos de segurança para proteger as pessoas e o próprio animal. Em seguida, foi solta em seu habitat natural.

O Corpo de Bombeiros orienta a população a manter distância ao encontrar animais silvestres e a não tentar capturá-los ou manuseá-los. A recomendação é acionar profissionais capacitados pelo número 193.

articles.title: TRE-PE manda restabelecer frota de ônibus e manter metrô gratuito | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão cita denúncias de falta de veículos na Imbiribeira e na Macaxeira e na linha Tiúma/Camaragibe. Descumprimento pode gerar multa diária de R$ 1 milhão.
articles.summary: Decisão cita denúncias de falta de veículos na Imbiribeira e na Macaxeira e na linha Tiúma/Camaragibe. Descumprimento pode gerar multa diária de R$ 1 milhão.
articles.body:
Fila de eleitores no Terminal Integrado da Macaxeira, na Zona Norte do Recife — Foto: Reprodução/WhatsApp

Faltando uma hora para o fim da votação deste domingo (25), o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Pernambuco (TRE-PE) determinou o restabelecimento imediato da frota de ônibus e do número de viagens previstos para o 2º turno das eleições no Grande Recife .

A decisão também obriga a Companhia Brasileira de Trens Urbanos (CBTU) a garantir a gratuidade e o funcionamento regular do metrô, das 5h às 23h. Ela foi tomada após denúncias de redução ou ausência de ônibus durante a votação.

A medida foi assinada pela desembargadora eleitoral Roberta Viana Jardim. Em caso de descumprimento, a multa diária é de R$ 1 milhão.

A decisão foi proferida após ação apresentada pela Federação Brasil da Esperança, formada por PT, PCdoB e PV, contra a Secretaria de Mobilidade e Infraestrutura de Pernambuco (Semobi), o Grande Recife Consórcio de Transporte e a CBTU.

A Autarquia de Trânsito e Transporte Urbano do Recife (CTTU) foi incluída no processo.

Na ação, a federação relatou que recebeu denúncias de falta ou redução drástica do serviço em linhas que deveriam operar durante o segundo turno.

Entre os problemas apontados estavam a ausência de ônibus na região da Imbiribeira, na Zona Sul; a falta ou redução de veículos na região da Macaxeira, na Zona Norte; e a ausência de veículos na linha 418, que liga Camaragibe a Tiúma, bairro de São Lourenço da Mata, na Região Metropolitana.

Eleitores denunciaram pelo Canal Globo dificuldades para usar o transporte público. Os casos foram de esperar de mais de uma hora em terminais e paradas de ônibus no Recife e em Camaragibe, na Região Metropolitana.

O Terminal Integrado da Macaxeira, no bairro de Dois Irmãos, na Zona Norte do Recife, usuários reclamaram de longas filas. Fotos encaminhadas ao WhatsApp da Globo mostram pessoas aglomeradas enquanto aguardam ônibus no terminal.

A ação também relatou superlotação nos terminais de integração. Segundo a federação, denúncias administrativas já haviam sido apresentadas ao Grande Recife Consórcio de Transporte e à CBTU, mas os problemas não tinham sido solucionados até o ajuizamento do processo.

A desembargadora determinou que o governo de Pernambuco, por meio da Semobi, e o Grande Recife Consórcio de Transporte garantam imediatamente a oferta gratuita das viagens previstas na relação oficial apresentada no processo, com o número de ônibus e de viagens estabelecido para o dia da eleição.

A ordem vale para todas as linhas abrangidas pela gratuidade, com atenção especial às regiões da Imbiribeira e da Macaxeira e à linha 418, entre Tiúma e Camaragibe. Os órgãos também devem tomar as providências necessárias junto às empresas de ônibus para restabelecer integralmente a frota e as viagens previstas.

A decisão reforça que o transporte público gratuito no dia da eleição não significa apenas deixar de cobrar passagem. O serviço também deve ser oferecido regularmente, com itinerários, quantidade de veículos e frequência compatíveis com os dias úteis.

No caso do metrô, a CBTU deve assegurar a gratuidade e cumprir o planejamento operacional informado ao TRE-PE. As linhas Centro e Sul devem funcionar normalmente, das 5h às 23h.

Os órgãos responsáveis também devem informar à Justiça Eleitoral, no prazo de uma hora, quais medidas foram efetivamente adotadas para cumprir a decisão. A determinação busca evitar a concentração de eleitores nos terminais de integração.

A desembargadora fixou multa diária de R$ 1 milhão em caso de descumprimento das determinações.

A responsabilidade pela penalidade foi dividida conforme as obrigações estabelecidas na decisão. O governo de Pernambuco e o Grande Recife Consórcio de Transporte respondem solidariamente pelo cumprimento da ordem relativa aos ônibus. Já a CBTU responde pelo cumprimento da determinação referente ao metrô.

A federação também havia pedido a prisão dos responsáveis por eventual descumprimento da ordem e a requisição de força policial, inclusive da Polícia Federal. A desembargadora, porém, negou esses pedidos por considerar que não havia elementos suficientes para justificar as medidas.

A decisão ressalta que eventuais consequências penais das condutas relatadas ainda podem ser apuradas pelos órgãos competentes.

articles.title: Bisavó de 83 anos faz questão de votar mesmo com balão de oxigênio  | G1
articles.standfirst: Maria do Rosário de Sousa Louzada foi acompanhada pelo filho e pela irmã até o local de votação, em Anápolis. Segundo a família, ela ficou chateada por não ter conseguido votar na eleição anterior, quando estava internada.
articles.summary: Maria do Rosário de Sousa Louzada votou em Anápolis.  Segundo a família, ela ficou chateada por não ter conseguido votar na eleição anterior, quando estava internada.
articles.body:
Uma bisavó de 83 anos fez questão de ir votar em Anápolis , na região central de Goiás, mesmo após um problema com o equipamento de oxigênio durante o trajeto até a seção eleitoral. Maria do Rosário de Sousa Louzada foi acompanhada pelo filho, Antônio Alex de Souza, e pela irmã, Raimunda, de 74 anos.

Segundo Antônio, a mãe sempre gostou de votar presencialmente e ficou chateada por não ter conseguido participar da eleição anterior, por estar.

“Ela sempre gostou de ir lá e votar presencial”, contou o filho.

Maria teve um acidente vascular cerebral (AVC) há cerca de 20 anos e também passou por uma cirurgia de ponte de safena, segundo Antônio, que é responsável pelos cuidados com a mãe.

No caminho até o local de votação, a família enfrentou um imprevisto. Segundo Antônio, uma peça do equipamento de oxigênio quebrou, e ele precisou voltar para casa para buscar outra e resolver o problema antes de continuar o trajeto. “Queria porque queria, não ia deixar”, disse Antônio sobre a vontade da mãe de ir votar.

Apesar da dificuldade, Maria conseguiu chegar ao local e participar da votação. O filho contou que a família precisou se organizar para garantir que ela pudesse sair de casa com o equipamento de oxigênio.

Idosa com vai votar com tanque de oxigênio — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/ Antônio Alex De Souza

A neta de Maria, Eveline Prado Souza Pacheco, de 33 anos, contou que a avó ficou chateada por não ter conseguido votar na eleição anterior, quando estava internada.

“Ela ficou bem chateada com isso de não ter ido. E graças a Deus ela teve mais essa oportunidade de poder votar, né? Ela ficou bem feliz”, afirmou Eveline.

Segundo a neta, Maria gosta de participar das atividades e de sair de casa, mas isso ficou mais difícil depois que ela passou a usar oxigênio. A família também não conseguiu mais levá-la ao estádio para acompanhar partidas de futebol.

Para Eveline, a disposição da avó também pode servir de exemplo para os mais jovens.

“A gente vê jovens que têm a plena disponibilidade de ir e não votam. Acho que realmente é um exemplo de cidadania mesmo”, disse.

A irmã de Maria, Raimunda, de 74 anos, também acompanhou a idosa na votação. De acordo com Antônio, as duas gostavam de votar juntas.

articles.title: 'Enquanto eu for viva, vou votar', diz idosa de 108 anos no 2º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Mesmo sem conseguir votar no primeiro turno devido à chuva, Maria dos Santos compareceu às urnas neste domingo, em Ponta Porã.
articles.summary: Mesmo sem conseguir votar no primeiro turno devido à chuva, Maria dos Santos compareceu às urnas neste domingo, em Ponta Porã.
articles.body:
Aos 108 anos, Maria dos Santos fez questão de votar no segundo turno das eleições de 2026 — Foto: Liniker Ribeiro/TV Morena

Aos 108 anos, Maria dos Santos fez questão de votar no segundo turno das eleições de 2026, neste domingo (25), em Ponta Porã . Acompanhada pela neta, de 28 anos, ela foi até o local de votação e aproveitou a ocasião para cumprir a prova de vida do Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS), necessária para a manutenção do benefício.

Maria contou à reportagem que não conseguiu votar no primeiro turno por causa da chuva forte. Desta vez, decidiu ir às urnas e participar da votação.

“Sou aposentada e tenho que fazer a prova de vida. Então, fui votar. No primeiro turno, não deu para eu ir porque estava chovendo muito. Mas hoje eu falei: ‘Vai dar para eu ir’. Fiz questão de votar e votei”, relatou.

Aos 108 anos, Maria afirma que pretende continuar votando enquanto puder. “Enquanto eu for viva, eu vou votar”, disse.

Natural da Paraíba, Maria deixou o estado aos 14 anos. Ela foi de carro com a neta até o local de votação. Segundo ela, o trajeto foi rápido e, quando percebeu, já estava de volta em casa.

Maria também disse esperar que as eleições contribuam para melhorar a convivência entre as pessoas. “Espero que melhore a convivência, que a gente se dê bem mais um pouco”, afirmou.

A neta, Mayara Almeida Silva, diz que vê na avó um exemplo de participação nas eleições.

“É bom levar ela como exemplo pros eleitores e de democracia. Toda vez que tem Eleição, pra prefeito e presidente, ela quer ir. Serve de exemplo pra mim também, porque eu mesmo, hoje cedo, estava com preguiça de ir votar e ela cedinho já estava acordada e na chuva mesmo ela foi toda faceira", conta.

Maria também deixou uma mensagem aos eleitores.

“Sempre votem e continuem votando, porque a nossa realidade é essa. Mas votar com fé e coragem”, declarou.

Maria dos Santos registrou o momento de votação, em Ponta Porã — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

articles.title: Votação em Portugal: adolescente brasileira é agredida em Lisboa | G1
articles.standfirst: Jovem andava em rua da capital portuguesa com camiseta vermelha e foi agredida com um soco por homem com camiseta amarela após deixar local de votação, segundo imprensa local. Embaixada do Brasil em Portugal confirmou episódio e disse que polícia abriu inquérito. Agressor fugiu.
articles.summary: Jovem andava em rua da capital portuguesa com camiseta vermelha e foi agredida com um soco por homem com camiseta amarela, segundo imprensa local.
articles.body:
Brasileiros votam no segundo turno das eleições em Lisboa, Portugal — Foto: ISIDRO GOMES/ATO PRESS/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

Uma adolescente brasileira foi agredida com um soco neste domingo (25) em uma rua de Lisboa, em Portugal, segundo a Embaixada do Brasil no país. Um homem de camiseta amarela do Brasil fez a agressão, de acordo com registros da imprensa portuguesa. A vítima vestia uma camiseta vermelha, ainda segundo os registros.

O embaixador do Brasil em Portugal, Alessandro Candeas, afirmou que o agressor fugiu, mas disse que a polícia de Lisboa foi acionada e abriu um inquérito para investigar o caso.

De acordo com Candeas, a jovem, uma brasileira de 17 anos, havia acabado de votar e caminhava na rua com sua família quando foi agredida por um homem na rua. Uma equipe da embaixada foi acionada por outros brasileiros que presenciaram a cena.

Adolescente brasileira é socorrida por bombeiro em Lisboa, em Portugal, após ser agredida com um soco após sair de local de votação, em 25 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/ Diário de Notícias

A jovem foi socorrida por bombeiros e levada a um hospital, de acordo com a Embaixada do Brasil em Portugal. Uma equipe do jornal "Diário de Notícias" disse ter registrado o momento em que a jovem era levada a uma ambulância que foi até o local ( veja na imagem acima ).

Vídeos que circulam nas redes sociais mostram um homem vestido com camiseta amarela, acompanhado de uma mulher, se afastando enquanto são acusados pela agressão.

A Embaixada do Brasil em Portugal não confirmou se o homem gravado era o agressor. O embaixador, no entanto, disse ter acionado a polícia, que recolheu as imagens e abriu um inquérito. Em entrevista ao Diário de Notícias, Candeas afirmou ainda que o episódio foi "muito grave" e "inaceitável".

articles.title: UBS Mogi das Cruzes: Unidades Vila Suíssa e Jundiaí fecham para obra | G1
articles.standfirst: Unidades da Vila Suíssa e da Vila Jundiaí terão pacientes transferidos temporariamente para outras da rede municipal, segundo a Prefeitura. Consultas agendadas serão mantidas, e as obras têm previsão de conclusão em maio de 2027.
articles.summary: Com obras até 2027, as UBSs Vila Suíssa e Vila Jundiaí em Mogi das Cruzes suspendem atendimentos locais, mas mantêm consultas agendadas em outras unidades da rede municipal.
articles.body:
UBS da Vila Suíssa, em Mogi das Cruzes, ficará fechada para reforma — Foto: Reprodução / PMMC

As Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBSs) da Vila Suíssa e da Vila Jundiaí, em Mogi das Cruzes , serão fechadas para reforma a partir desta segunda-feira (26). Durante as obras, os pacientes serão atendidos em outras unidades da rede municipal.

Segundo a Prefeitura, as consultas agendadas serão mantidas durante o período de reforma. No entanto, a administração municipal não informou, no comunicado divulgado, quais postos receberão os pacientes das duas unidades.

A previsão é que as obras sejam concluídas em maio de 2027. Segundo a Prefeitura, as reformas têm como objetivo “modernizar a estrutura física das unidades, proporcionando mais conforto, segurança e melhores condições de atendimento aos usuários e de trabalho aos profissionais de saúde”.

Ao todo, a cidade conta conta com 18 UBSs, que oferecem consultas nas áreas de clínica geral, pediatria, ginecologia e obstetrícia, além de atendimento em saúde mental.

As unidades também oferecem acolhimento inicial em saúde mental, sem necessidade de agendamento, e encaminhamento para serviços especializados da rede municipal, quando necessário.

As reformas fazem parte de um programa da Prefeitura que prevê melhorias em 16 Unidades Básicas de Saúde de Mogi das Cruzes.

Até o momento, seis unidades já passaram por reformas e foram entregues à população: Jardim Maricá, Braz Cubas, Mineração, Jardim Ivete, Santo Ângelo e Jundiapeba.

Na segunda-feira (26), a UBS Vila Nova Aparecida também será reaberta após passar por obras. Já a UBS Jardim Camila segue em reforma, com previsão de conclusão em dezembro de 2026.

As próximas etapas do programa incluem as unidades Vila Natal, Ponte Grande, Alto do Ipiranga, Vila Moraes, Vila da Prata e Santa Tereza. As datas de início das obras ainda serão definidas.

UBS Braz Cubas em Mogi das Cruzes — Foto: Divulgação / PMMC

As consultas com clínico geral, pediatra e ginecologista devem ser agendadas pelo telefone 160, do Sistema Integrado de Saúde (SIS).

Além das 18 UBSs convencionais, o município conta com a UBS Jardim Universo, que possui um modelo diferente de funcionamento e oferece atendimento de urgência 24 horas.

Entenda a diferença entre UPA, UBS e USF

Além das UBSs, a rede municipal de saúde soma a serviços como Unidades de Pronto Atendimento (UPAs), Unidade de Saúde da Família (USFs) e unidades 24 horas.

Cada equipamento atende um tipo de caso — de situações graves até consultas de rotina —, e saber qual unidade procurar em cada situação pode ajudar a agilizar o atendimento e garantir o encaminhamento adequado para cada tipo de necessidade.

Lula recebeu 141.263 votos ( 59,66% ), enquanto Flávio teve 95.499 votos ( 40,34% ), segundo boletins de urna divulgados pelo TSE até o momento.

Os dois candidatos ampliaram suas votações em relação ao primeiro turno. Na ocasião, Lula recebeu 95.442 votos, contra 48.874 de Flávio. O petista levou em 25 países com urnas na região no primeiro turno. Já o senador venceu em 2: Grécia e Ucrânia.

articles.title: Chuvas na região de Itapetininga: caminhão tomba em Ribeirão Branco | G1
articles.standfirst: Veículo estava no bairro Cachoeira, que sofreu com alagamentos durante chuva na madrugada; temporal causou estragos em diferentes cidades da região de Itapetininga durante este domingo (25).
articles.summary: As fortes chuvas na região de Itapetininga causaram o tombamento de um caminhão em Ribeirão Branco e deixaram dezenas de desabrigados em Guareí neste domingo.
articles.body:
Ponte cedeu com peso de caminhão carregado de madeira em Ribeirão Branco (SP) — Foto: Defesa Civil / Divulgação

Um caminhão carregado com toras tombou ao atravessar uma ponte de madeira que cedeu neste domingo (25), no bairro Cachoeira, em Ribeirão Branco (SP). Segundo a Defesa Civil, a estrutura foi danificada durante a chuva que atingiu a região durante a madrugada e, por isso, não aguentou o peso do veículo na travessia.

Não há informações de pessoas feridas neste acidente. Outras cidades da região também registraram ocorrências com enchentes e quedas de árvore após o temporal.

Em Itapetininga (SP), o transbordamento do Ribeirão dos Cavalos provocou alagamentos em ruas próximas e atingiu residências na Rua Salomão Abid, na Vila Santa Isabel. Duas pessoas estão desabrigadas e foram acolhidas em um abrigo municipal provisório.

As fortes chuvas também provocaram enxurradas em Itapeva (SP), principalmente na região da Avenida Roberto Geminiani, passando pela Avenida Paulina de Moraes, Prefeitura e Mercado Produtor. Alguns veículos foram atingidos.

Chuva causa alagamentos em Itapetininga (SP) — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

A Rodovia SP-129, que liga Tatuí (SP) a Boituva (SP), foi interditada na altura do km 25 por causa das chuvas. Equipes da Defesa Civil e do Departamento de Estradas de Rodagem (DER) estão no local.

O Rio das Pedras também apresentou aumento significativo do nível durante a madrugada deste domingo (25), principalmente no bairro dos Fragas, próximo ao Parque Ecológico Maria Tuca.

Segundo a Defesa Civil Municipal de Guareí (SP), entre 30 e 40 casas foram atingidas por alagamentos na região central da cidade, afetando aproximadamente 60 pessoas.

O Rio Guareí subiu quase dois metros acima do nível normal. O município registrou cerca de 100 milímetros de chuva nas últimas horas, volume equivalente ao esperado para todo o mês, segundo a Defesa Civil.

Guareí (SP) fica com pontos alagados após chuva forte e cheia em rio — Foto: Jacutinga Notícias

Em Tietê (SP), uma cratera se abriu no fim da Rua Alfredo Melaré, no bairro Emílio Gardenal, após as fortes chuvas. A força da água atingiu uma área de pastagem próxima e derrubou dois postes de energia elétrica e três árvores de grande porte.

Três residências ficaram sem energia elétrica. Equipes da Defesa Civil e da Elektro estão no local para eliminar os riscos e realizar os reparos necessários.

articles.title: Jovem tetraplégica vota pela primeira vez no 2º turno em Indaiatuba | G1
articles.standfirst: Luísa Marins sofreu acidente aos 17 anos e usa cadeira de rodas motorizada. Ela conseguiu votar neste domingo (25), em Indaiatuba (SP), após enfrentar dificuldades de acesso no primeiro turno.
articles.summary: Luísa Marins, jovem tetraplégica de Indaiatuba, superou obstáculos de acessibilidade para votar pela primeira vez no 2º turno e defendeu a importância do SUS.
articles.body:
Aos 22 anos, Luísa Marins votou pela primeira vez neste domingo (25), durante o segundo turno das eleições de 2026, em Indaiatuba (SP).

Tetraplégica desde os 17 anos, quando sofreu um acidente, a jovem utiliza uma cadeira de rodas motorizada e fez questão de comparecer à Fundação Indaiatubana de Educação e Cultura (Fiec) para exercer o direito ao voto.

Luísa tentou votar no primeiro turno, mas a chuva e as dificuldades para sair do carro e chegar à seção eleitoral impediram sua participação . Desta vez, com condições mais favoráveis, conseguiu acessar o prédio e utilizar a urna eletrônica sem dificuldades.

"Minha primeira eleição, eu estou bem feliz. Eu vim votar no primeiro turno, mas acabou que eu não consegui, me arrependi e estou aqui para fazer a diferença com meu voto", contou.

Segundo a jovem, a estrutura da Fiec facilitou o deslocamento com a cadeira de rodas motorizada e permitiu que ela votasse com autonomia.

"Foi bem tranquilo. Hoje não está chovendo, eu consegui descer do carro tranquilamente. Aqui dentro também da Fiec é bem acessível e foi tranquilo na urna também para eu conseguir apertar os botões", relatou.

Luísa Marins, de 22 anos, que é tetraplégica, votou pela primeira vez no segundo turno das eleições 2026, na FIEC, em Indaiatuba (SP) — Foto: Juliano Amorim

A mãe de Luísa, Moira Cuchinaro, acompanhou a filha na votação. Ela contou que o acidente provocou uma lesão na região cervical que inicialmente deixou Luísa sem movimentos do pescoço para baixo.

Cinco meses após a alta hospitalar, a jovem iniciou um tratamento de reabilitação no Instituto Lucy Montoro, em São Paulo (SP), onde permaneceu por cinco meses. Atualmente, Luísa continua sendo acompanhada pela unidade do instituto em Campinas (SP).

"Ela passou por cinco meses de tratamento lá e até hoje é acompanhada aqui em Campinas, pelo Instituto Lucy Montoro. E isso é graças ao SUS", afirmou.

Moira também explicou que a filha recebe pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) sondas utilizadas em um procedimento necessário aos seus cuidados diários.

Para a mãe, a primeira votação de Luísa representa não apenas uma conquista pessoal, mas também a importância de garantir que pessoas com deficiência tenham condições de participar das decisões políticas .

"É importantíssimo, pela democracia, que todos tenham o direito e a possibilidade de votar. Então é necessário que essa política pública que faz com que a Luísa possa chegar até a urna seja mantida e preservada", destacou.

articles.title: Report: Iran's Revolutionary Guards attack Kurdish positions in Iraq
articles.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has launched an attack on Kurdish positions in northern Iraq near the border with Iran, the Mehr news agency, which...
articles.body:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has launched an attack on Kurdish positions in northern Iraq near the border with Iran, the Mehr news agency, which is close to the government in Tehran, reported on Sunday.

"The headquarters of the Komala terrorist and separatist group in Iraq's Balisan was targeted in a drone operation by the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) Ground Forces overnight, within the framework of pre-emptive offensive measures," Mehr reported on its website.

There were initially no reports of casualties.

Tehran classifies many Kurdish groups in Iraq as "terrorist groups." According to human rights advocates, the Kurdish minority in Iran is also subject to repression.

In recent years, the IRGC has repeatedly attacked Kurdish targets in Iraq. Tensions along the border have increased since the start of the war with the United States and Israel.

The Kurds are an ethnic group with an estimated population of 30 million, living primarily in Iraq, Iran, Syria and Turkey. For decades, they have fought for a state of their own and have long faced persecution and repression in both Iraq and Iran.

The autonomous Kurdish region in Iraq emerged following the overthrow of dictator Saddam Hussein in 2003.

articles.title: Storm Boelo sees passenger plane leave runway at Birmingham Airport
articles.summary: Storm Boleo is the second named storm of the season, and follows Storm Austen.
articles.body:
High winds caused a passenger plane to momentarily leave the runway at Birmingham Airport as Storm Boelo brought disruption across the West Midlands.

Jet2 said flight LS1310 from Venice moved off the runway after landing on Sunday afternoon due to "exceptional weather conditions" caused by the storm.

The airline said the aircraft immediately returned to the runway and later taxied to its stand, with all passengers disembarking normally.

Railway services have also been disrupted across the region, with trees blocking lines and causing cancellations.

A spokesperson for Jet2 said: "Flight LS1310 from Venice to Birmingham temporarily moved off the runway after landing at Birmingham Airport earlier this afternoon, due to exceptional weather conditions caused by Storm Boelo.

"The aircraft immediately returned to the runway and has now taxied to the stand. We can confirm that everyone has disembarked as normal."

CrossCountry trains between Birmingham New Street and Nuneaton have been cancelled due to a tree on the line. The operator said tickets could be used on other services and it had requested rail replacement buses.

West Midlands Railway services between Four Oaks, Birmingham, and Lichfield Trent Valley, Staffordshire, were cancelled in both directions due to a downed tree, although the line has since reopened.

Transport for Wales services between Cardiff and Shrewsbury have been cancelled, while disruption has also been reported between Aberystwyth and Shrewsbury.

Elsewhere, a tree fell onto a car overnight in Moor Street, Coventry.

Hundreds of homes were left without power on Sunday morning, with power down in Bromyard, Herefordshire, and Drakes Broughton and Tilesford, Worcestershire.

On Sunday afternoon, more than 100 homes in Burford, Worcestershire also experienced power cuts, as well as more 77 homes in Bickenhill, Birmingham, 109 in Ryton-on-Dunsmore, Warwickshire, and 141 properties in Upper Cotton, Staffordshire.

Flood alerts across the region include the Severn Vyrnwy confluence in Shropshire, and the River Wye in Herefordshire.

Warwickshire Fire and Rescue Service said it had been attending "multiple calls" due to gazebos and other garden items being blown away and causing damage to electrical infrastructure, like solar panels.

"To avoid further incidents, please double check that everything in your garden is secure, and put away anything that might get taken by the strong wind," it said on Facebook.

In Shropshire, Forestry England said its Haughmond Hill site would remain shut on Sunday.

Severn Valley Rescue, an animal rescue centre near Bridgnorth, said it would close, due to "high winds, fallen trees and intermittent electricity" threatening health and safety.

All National Trust sites in Herefordshire are shut on Sunday - with the firm saying they would reopen on Monday after post-storm checks.

Wild Zoological Park in Bobbington, Wolverhampton, said it would close after being "absolutely battered by wind".

In a post on social media, it said: "We've got falling branches and a keeper has already been hit (but is ok)."

articles.title: Opposition leader María Machado returns to Venezuela
articles.summary: Machado had left the country just a month before the US government seized Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.
articles.body:
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile.

"I am here. With you," Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated prior efforts to re-enter the country came to no avail.

In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President Nicolás Maduro.

The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy Rodríguez, as leader and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal which granted very favourable terms to the US.

Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands.

Her ally, former presidential candidate Edmundo González, confirmed her arrival, writing in a statement: "I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil."

"Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!" González said.

He added that he will soon join Machado in Venezuela to advance the country "toward freedom".

An advisor to Machado said in September that over the previous few weeks Machado had attempted seven times to return to Venezuela, but was denied each time. There have been reports that the US was involved in delaying her return, which it has denied.

It's unclear what Machado plans to do next now that she's back, but she has previously said she would run for president again if an election were held . Her ability to return to her country was always contingent on approval from the Trump administration, which it appears has now been granted.

A staunch supporter of democracy, Machado won an independent presidential primary election - held outside the Maduro government's official election authority - in 2023, earning more than 90% of the vote.

Despite winning the primary, Maduro's government barred Machado from running for office, accusing her of fraud and tax violations. Machado denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated. She spent her final days in the country hiding in safehouses before her fleeing to Norway to accept the Nobel Prize.

In the 2024 election, Machado's ally González ran in her place against Maduro.

The electoral authority, which is closely aligned with the government, declared Maduro the winner without making detailed voting tallies public.

The opposition argued that González won the election, not Maduro, uploading copies of the voting tallies as evidence.

Maduro was removed from the country by US forces in January, and is currently jailed in New York where he faces drugs, weapons and torture charges. He has pleaded not guilty.

A spokesman for Machado called her return "a major step toward a democratic transition and free, fair, and verifiable presidential elections in the near future".

"We thank President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the US Government, Congress, and allied governments for their continued leadership and support," her spokesperson, David Smolansky, added.

Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump said, "I don't know anything about" her return, and added that he hoped she was "safe".

"I think she's a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel Prize, so how can I say anything else? And I hope she's safe," he said.

In January, Machado visited the White House and gifted her Nobel prize award to Trump . The committee that issues the prize had said "it cannot be revoked, shared, or transferred to others".

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised his country's role in securing her return through political reconciliation talks.

"The conditions allowing for the safe return of Ms Machado to Venezuela is the direct result of the US supported reconciliation talks which has already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile," he posted on X.

He added: "We expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy."

articles.title: London couple’s kombucha brand MOMO moves into a 16,000-square-foot brewery, aiming to increase production from 60,000 to 300,000 bottles a week
articles.summary: MOMO, a kombucha brand founded by a London couple in their kitchen in 2018, took over a new 16,000-square-foot site in Herne Hill, South London.
articles.body: MOMO, a kombucha brand founded by a London couple in their kitchen in 2018, took over a new 16,000-square-foot site in Herne Hill, South London. The move was set to bring the business back near its roots, just a couple of minutes from where founders Josh and Lisa Puddle started the company.According to Southwark News, the Great Taste Award-winning kombucha had been brewed at New Covent Garden Market for seven years.The new site, formerly occupied by Brixton Brewery, included dedicated fermentation space, a laboratory and a kitchen. The South London business said the new location and equipment would increase production capacity from 60,000 bottles per week to 300,000 bottles per week, giving the business more room to innovate and expand as of July 2026.MOMO announced a move into a 16,000-square-foot brewery to expand productionMOMO took over the former Brixton Brewery site in Herne Hill, close to where Josh and Lisa Puddle started their business from their home in 2018. The company had spent seven years brewing its kombucha at New Covent Garden Market.Co-founder Josh Puddle said the move would bring the business back to its south-east London roots. He said, “Lisa and I started Momo with a clear aim to produce the UK’s best-tasting and highest-quality kombucha. That has been the number one pillar of our strategy and always will be”.“I believe the kombucha category in the UK is where craft beer was 20 years ago, and it feels fitting to be giving this former beer brewery a healthy facelift”.What flavours did MOMO offer in its £4.50 kombucha rangeKombucha is fermented tea that has been around for thousands of years. articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has drawn a rare rebuke from the Bank of Israel after suggesting that cryptocurrency and blockchain technology could help the country circumvent potential international sanctions.In an interview with Israel's Channel 10 economic network on Friday, Netanyahu said he was preparing for a scenario in which foreign governments could impose sanctions on Israeli banks. “There could be sanctions, and sanctions on banks so you need to set up a bypass economy,” he said, confirming that he was referring to cryptocurrency when asked directly. His main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, described the plan as “madness”, warning that what he called the “BibiCoin policy” could drive companies abroad and weaken national security. Opposition leader Yair Lapid accused Netanyahu of making alarming promises to voters about the country's economic future.The controversy comes as Netanyahu faces pressure over both security and the economy. articles.title: In 2020, an Alabama lawyer closed her practice, sold her home and moved to care for her sick parents after they offered a share of their condo; six years later, the state's top court upheld the cancellation of her deed
articles.summary: An Alabama lawyer who left her legal career to care for her sick parents has lost her claim to part ownership of their coastal condominium.
articles.body: An Alabama lawyer who left her legal career to care for her sick parents has lost her claim to part ownership of their coastal condominium. The Alabama Supreme Court upheld a decision cancelling the deed that had given her a share of the property. The court upheld a lower court ruling that voided the property transfer made in 2020. It found that state laws protecting elderly property owners take priority over the personal sacrifices family members make in exchange for property. The decision in Schumpert v. Wallace ends a legal dispute involving former lawyer Holly Schumpert. She moved to Orange Beach, Alabama, after her parents, Alton and Patsy Schumpert, became ill and offered her half ownership of their home.Abandoning practice for family dutyIn late 2020, after both her parents suffered serious health problems, Holly Schumpert closed her law practice in Tennessee, sold her house and moved to Alabama to care for them full-time. In October 2020, Alton and Patsy signed a warranty deed giving Holly a 50 per cent share of their Orange Beach condominium. The agreement was based on her promise to provide ongoing personal support and care. However, the property was already held in a family trust set up by her parents. The deed giving Holly a share did not mention the trust or state that Alton and Patsy were signing the document as trustees. Holly later testified that she did not know the trust officially owned the coastal home when the deed was signed. Holly lived at the Orange Beach property and cared for her parents until early 2022. As their physical health improved and they became more independent, relationships within the family began to worsen. In July 2022, Holly discovered that her brother, Alton Schumpert Jr., planned to move into the condominium. She then left the property and returned to Tennessee.State law protects elderly grantorsAfter relations within the family broke down, Alton and Patsy filed a lawsuit in a local circuit court. They asked the court to cancel the 2020 deed under Section 8-9-12 of the Alabama Code. The law states that a property transfer can be cancelled at the property owner's request if a key part of the agreement involves a promise to care for the owner for the rest of their life. The rule is intended to protect older and vulnerable property owners who transfer their assets in return for promised care. Holly asked the court to change the deed to show that her parents had acted as trustees. She also filed counterclaims alleging fraud. She argued that she had kept her side of the agreement by giving up her legal career and making major financial sacrifices to care for her parents. In May 2025, the trial court ruled against Holly. It declared the 2020 warranty deed completely invalid and confirmed that she had no legal ownership of the Orange Beach condominium. Holly then appealed to the Alabama Supreme Court.Supreme Court upholds deed annulmentThe Alabama Supreme Court unanimously upheld the lower court's decision. The justices ruled that Section 8-9-12 gives parents the legal right to cancel property transfers made in exchange for care, even if the person receiving the property has already provided some of the promised support. In its written opinion, the court acknowledged the personal sacrifices Holly had made for her parents. However, it said the law left little room for the court to make an exception based on her circumstances. "We recognize the concerns Holly raises in her brief regarding the devotion she showed to her parents and the personal sacrifices she made on their behalf," the Supreme Court of Alabama noted in its written opinion. "Nevertheless, in enacting § 8-9-12, the Legislature made a clear public-policy choice to protect elderly and vulnerable property owners. Our role is to enforce that legislative choice." Alton Schumpert died in October 2024. After his death, Alton Jr. was appointed the personal representative of his estate and took his place in the legal proceedings alongside Patsy. The court's ruling leaves the 2020 warranty deed cancelled. Holly retains no ownership share or financial interest in the condominium, while the property remains under the ownership of her parents' estate and the surviving family interests.You use AI every day. articles.title: Lula vs Flavio Bolsonaro: 5 key issues shaping Brazil’s neck-and-neck election
articles.summary: Brazilian voters are heading to the ballot box for a closely contested presidential runoff between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing
articles.body: Brazilian voters are heading to the ballot box for a closely contested presidential runoff between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. With polls indicating a neck-and-neck race, the outcome will shape the direction of Latin America's largest economy and its relations with the United States.The election pits Lula, a veteran left-wing leader seeking another term, against Bolsonaro, who has courted US President Donald Trump and promised a shift in Brazil's economic and foreign policies. Flavio Bolsonaro secured more than 2.2 million votes more than Lula in the first round earlier this month, although turnout and support from voters who backed other candidates could prove decisive.The campaign has centred on rising living costs, crime, corruption and mounting pressure on public finances. Foreign policy has also emerged as a significant issue following Washington's tariffs on Brazilian goods in 2025.Cost of living, crime and corruption take centre stageEconomic pressures have emerged as a key challenge for Lula, with inflation remaining above the central bank's 3% target. More than two-thirds of respondents in an August Quaest poll said their purchasing power had declined compared with the previous year. Lula has promised to control inflation and gradually reduce borrowing costs, while Bolsonaro has proposed stabilising public debt to bring interest rates down.Public finances are another major concern. Brazil's public debt rose to 82.9% of gross domestic product during Lula's current term, while high interest rates have added to the financial strain on households and businesses. Bolsonaro has pledged to improve the primary fiscal balance by 1.5% of GDP within 18 months. Lula, meanwhile, has targeted an effective primary surplus of around 1.3% of GDP by 2030.Crime and corruption have also featured prominently. Bolsonaro has promised maximum-security prisons and chemical castration for serious sexual offences. Lula has proposed expanding federal prison capacity to hold gang leaders while investing in poorer communities to limit organised crime.Both candidates face scrutiny over corruption allegations involving their circles. Bolsonaro is under investigation over alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion linked to money received from disgraced former banker Daniel Vorcaro to produce a film about his father. He denies wrongdoing. Lula's son is also being investigated in cases involving alleged influence-peddling, corruption and fraud, and has denied the allegations.Trump ties and Brazil's global directionForeign policy has emerged as a major dividing line. Bolsonaro wants to strengthen relations with the US, Argentina and Israel, arguing that ties with these countries have deteriorated. He has also highlighted opportunities for closer economic cooperation with Washington, including in rare earth minerals, an area where Brazil holds substantial reserves.Lula, by contrast, has advocated multilateralism and stronger ties with the Mercosur bloc and BRICS nations. He has criticised Trump's trade measures and raised concerns about US intervention in Brazil's affairs.The result could mark a significant ideological shift for Brazil. While Bolsonaro has promised an amnesty for his father, who is under house arrest over his conviction for attempting a coup, Lula has portrayed his rival's political camp as a threat to democratic institutions.You use AI every day. articles.title: Man killed by falling tree as Storm Boelo leaves 160,000 properties without power
articles.summary: An amber wind warning will remain until Sunday evening as severe weather continues to batter the UK.
articles.body:
A 60-year-old man has died after being hit by a falling tree in southern Scotland as Storm Boelo continues to bring severe weather to the UK.

Police Scotland said the man was pronounced dead at the scene following the incident near Castle Douglas in Dumfries and Galloway at about 10:30 on Sunday.

The harsh weather battering the UK had left 161,400 properties without power as of 15:00 GMT on Sunday afternoon, the Energy Networks Association (ENA) said.

Those still without electricity have faced delays as the dangerous conditions were "limiting network engineers' opportunities to safely start the work", the ENA added.

During Storm Boelo and the earlier Storm Austen, which hit the UK on Friday, 838,700 properties across the country faced power cuts, according to the ENA.

Wind gusts peaked on Sunday morning at 85mph in Machrihanish, in Argyll and Bute, and 84mph in both Stornoway in the Outer Hebrides, and Capel Curig in north Wales.

An amber wind warning issued by the Met Office will remain in place until 21:00 on Sunday across Scotland and parts of northern England.

A yellow warning that also covers other areas of the north of England, including Liverpool, Manchester, Leeds, Sheffield and Newcastle-upon-Tyne, as well as parts of the East and West Midlands and North Wales, is in place until 21:00 on Sunday.

The Met Office has urged people to "stay indoors as much as possible", adding: "If you do go out, try not to walk, or shelter, close to buildings and trees."

The strongest gusts have continued to spread eastwards across the UK on Sunday.

Four flood warnings have been issued for parts of England and Wales on Sunday, while there are 17 flood warnings in place in Scotland.

High rainfall totals have been recorded in the Scottish Highlands, peaking in Cluanie Inn which received 130mm.

Scottish government ministers and officials gathered on Sunday afternoon to discuss the impact of Storm Boelo.

In a statement, the Scottish government said while conditions may ease later on Sunday, there is potential for adverse weather to return in the coming days.

In Aberfeldy, Perth and Kinross, two women were taken to hospital after being struck by a fallen tree at around 12:50 GMT on Sunday, police said.

The towns of the Clyde coast in Scotland have been hit particularly hard by the severe weather. The main Skelmorlie to Largs road has been badly damaged and a number of businesses in Largs were flooded overnight on Saturday.

In Gourock, a boat ended up on the side of the road and there have been reports of power being out in Girvan all throughout Sunday.

In Dumbarton, on the north bank of the River Clyde, Muhammad Zubair Ashraf's mobile phone shop was flooded overnight.

He estimated between £5,000 and £10,000 of damage was caused and said he was "heartbroken" at the scale of the losses.

Travel has been affected across the country, with police in Scotland warning against unnecessary road journeys.

Ferry services have been impacted, some flights to and from Belfast, Glasgow, Aberdeen and Dublin airports have been cancelled, and train services across the UK have faced disruption.

"I'm here. With you all," Machado wrote on social media, announcing her return for the first time since December. Her homecoming comes as Venezuela remains under the leadership of acting President Delcy Rodríguez, a longtime Maduro ally backed by the Trump administration, with no presidential election scheduled. Machado spent much of 2025 in hiding after being briefly detained following an opposition protest that January. She later secretly left Venezuela and resurfaced in Norway in December to receive the Nobel Peace Prize. articles.title: 1,200km reach, Western parts: How Russia’s new Filin missile adds to Ukraine’s air defence woes
articles.summary: Russia has begun using a new cruise missile, the Filin, against Ukraine, adding to Moscow’s growing arsenal of relatively inexpensive long-range weapons
articles.body: Russia has begun using a new cruise missile, the Filin, against Ukraine, adding to Moscow’s growing arsenal of relatively inexpensive long-range weapons designed to stretch Kyiv’s air defences. The missile combines a Russian-made jet engine with electronic components linked to American and Chinese manufacturers, according to Ukraine’s military intelligence agency, HUR, as reported by Kyiv Post.The weapon reportedly entered combat use in late summer 2026. Its emergence highlights Russia’s efforts to develop cheaper strike systems capable of reaching targets deep inside Ukrainian territory, potentially complicating Kyiv’s efforts to intercept repeated waves of drones and missiles.On October 22, HUR released an interactive 3D model, technical specifications and a component database on its War&Sanctions portal. According to Militarnyi, the agency’s findings indicate that the Filin combines standardised electronics and some 3D-printed components with a Russian propulsion system. Its advertised performance, however, has not been independently verified. US electronics, Chinese navigation and Russian firepowerAccording to Kyiv Post, HUR identified 35 electronic components associated with US manufacturers and 22 linked to Chinese manufacturers. The agency said the electronics resemble those found in other Russian missiles and drones, with standardised designs across different onboard units and circuit boards that could help simplify production.The missile was developed by Moscow-based NPO Molniya, part of Russia’s Tactical Missiles Corporation. Its 3.5-metre-long fuselage and three-metre wingspan are made from carbon fibre and fibreglass composites, while some structural parts are manufactured using 3D printing, Militarnyi reported.The Filin uses a Russian-made R500 turbojet engine manufactured by Reynolds LLC. Its onboard equipment is assembled by St Petersburg-based PLAZ LLC, which is also involved in producing electronics for Russia’s Garpiya attack drones, according to the Long War Journal.For navigation, HUR identified a Chinese-made inertial navigation system and a 16-channel Kometa antenna designed to improve resistance to electronic warfare interference. The missile launches from a ground-based platform using a solid-propellant booster and reportedly carries either a 50-kg or 100-kg warhead.Russian-advertised specifications cited by HUR put its maximum speed at 800 kmph and its range at up to 1,200 km. The missile can reportedly fly at extremely low altitudes or reach heights of six kilometres, according to Kyiv Post. A cheaper weapon as Ukraine’s air defences face pressureThe Filin fits into a broader Russian push towards relatively inexpensive, mass-producible long-range weapons that complement more sophisticated systems such as the Kh-101 and Kalibr cruise missiles.The Long War Journal reported that Ukraine-based analyst Rob Lee said in August that Russia planned to procure more than 1,000 Filin missiles before the end of the year. However, the publication noted that the weapon had yet to see widespread use, leaving the status of those reported procurement plans uncertain.The development comes as Ukraine faces sustained aerial attacks. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy recently said Russia had launched nearly 2,300 strike drones, 48 missiles and around 1,600 guided bombs in a single week, damaging infrastructure and civilian facilities across nine regions.Kyiv has repeatedly urged Western allies to accelerate deliveries of air defence interceptors. At the same time, Zelenskyy has said Ukrainian, Russian and US negotiators were expected to hold technical-level talks in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November.

articles.title: An 80-ton boulder that had hung above visitors at New Hampshire's Polar Caves since the park opened in 1922 collapsed on the final day of the 2026 season, smashing a walkway but injuring no one
articles.summary: An 80-ton granite boulder known as the Mysterious Hanging Boulder collapsed at Polar Caves Park in Rumney, New Hampshire, crushing a wooden walkway on the
articles.body: An 80-ton granite boulder known as the Mysterious Hanging Boulder collapsed at Polar Caves Park in Rumney, New Hampshire, crushing a wooden walkway on the final day of the park's 2026 operating season. The huge rock had stuck out from a granite wall since the park first opened in 1922. It fell on 18 October, but no one was injured. The collapse happened on the day the attraction was due to close for the season, avoiding the risk to thousands of tourists who usually walk beneath the landmark during the busy months. Park managers confirmed that the falling boulder smashed part of a wooden walkway and its safety railings along the main hiking trail. The damage has blocked access to part of the path.A century of precarious balanceThe boulder was one of the main attractions at the privately owned park, which opened 104 years ago after glacial caves formed during the last ice age were discovered. For generations, visitors had used the rock as a popular background for photographs. It hung directly above a footbridge and provided shade for hikers walking beneath it as they made their way through narrow granite passages and fields of boulders. Although the rock looked as if it could fall at any moment, it had stayed firmly wedged in place since guided tours at the site began in the early 1920s.Geological factors behind the collapseGeologists examining the collapse have pointed to several possible natural causes. These include gravity, the gradual wearing away of the rock and repeated freezing and thawing caused by the weather in northern New England. In mountain areas with changing temperatures, water can seep into tiny cracks in rock faces. When the water freezes, it expands and puts pressure on the surrounding stone. Over many years, this process can widen the cracks and weaken large rock formations. The balance between the boulder's weight and the granite shelf supporting it may have gradually weakened until the rock finally broke free. Park officials told The Boston Globe that visitor safety remains their main concern. Engineers and ground crews are checking the surrounding granite walls and the area covered by fallen debris. They will use the results to decide how the hiking trail can be changed safely. The collapse is similar to another major loss of a natural landmark in New Hampshire. In May 2003, the Old Man of the Mountain, a famous granite formation on Cannon Mountain in Franconia Notch, collapsed after thousands of years of exposure to the weather.Reassessing trail infrastructureThe boulder fell as the park was preparing to close for the winter. This gave maintenance crews the chance to secure the damaged area without interrupting visits from the public. The damage was limited to the trail structures directly beneath the falling rock. The impact crushed the wooden frame of the raised walkway and broke the nearby protective railings. Park managers said inspections of the nearby cliffs would continue throughout the winter closure. The planned work includes clearing the damaged section of the trail, repairing the destroyed footbridges and checking that the surrounding rock faces are stable. Officials intend to complete the safety checks and repairs before the park reopens to visitors for the 2027 spring season.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2022, Chloe Hurst took a seasonal job on a remote Isle of Man island; she woke at 5 a.m. to ring birds as supply boats were delayed for weeks
articles.summary: Discover the challenges and rewards of island living as Chloe Hurst shares her experience working at the Calf of Man Bird Observatory. Learn about bird ringing, isolation, and the beauty of nature in this unique job.
articles.body: Most jobs come with a nearby shop, a canteen and a daily commute. Chloe Hurst's seasonal role on the Calf of Man was different. In 2022, she worked as a warden on the rocky island, which covers about 600 acres off the southern coast of the Isle of Man. Manx National Heritage owns the island, while Manx Wildlife Trust operates its bird observatory. The reserve supports bird monitoring and other conservation work. Manx National Heritage's official information about the Calf provides details about the island and its facilities.Hurst's experience shows both the demands and the rewards of remote conservation work. Her day began at 5 a.m. with bird ringing, followed by wildlife surveys, habitat management and other practical tasks. Daily life also meant adapting to limited food supplies, short weekly showers and deliveries that could be delayed for two to three weeks in bad weather. She returned in 2024 as a paid estate warden. Manx National Heritage records that about 33 species of seabirds breed on the island each year.Getting to the CalfTravel to the Calf normally depends on small boats. In a 2024 interview with The Independent, Hurst said she discovered the opportunity in 2022 while working at the Cornish Seal Sanctuary in Gweek. She applied through the Manx Wildlife Trust website after learning about the warden role. The Trust operates the bird observatory, while Manx National Heritage owns the island. Crossings from Port St Mary and Port Erin can take up to 40 minutes, depending on the vessel. Sailings depend on weather, tides and the availability of boat operators, and trips must be booked in advance. Manx National Heritage's visitor guide explains the access arrangements and warns that crossings can be cancelled if conditions are unsuitable.The warden team consists of four people, two focused on bird work and two on estate duties. They stay in a farmhouse with an attached hostel that can accommodate up to eight overnight guests during summer. That figure refers to the hostel's overnight capacity, not the total number of people who can visit the island during the day. Hurst said she had seen around 40 people on the island at once during the open season. There is no pub or shop. Rainwater is collected in large tanks and filtered for drinking, so water use is closely monitored and showers are limited to once a week. A generator and battery bank power the shower and dryer, while internet access can be slow.A day that starts at 5 a.m.Once on the island, the birds set the pace of the day. Bird ringing involves catching a bird, fitting a small metal ring with a unique number to one leg, recording its species, age, sex, wing length and weight, and then releasing it. On the Calf, birds are caught in fine mist nets or Heligoland traps and are normally processed within a minute or two so they can be released safely. The ringing programme began in 1959. By the start of the 2020 season, more than 275,000 birds representing 184 species had been ringed, according to Manx Wildlife Trust's official Calf of Man Bird Observatory information.The purpose of ringing has changed over time. Early work focused on establishing where birds travelled, while the modern emphasis includes monitoring populations and understanding changes in their numbers. Records from the Calf show that the average spring arrival of blackcaps advanced by about one week per decade between 1959 and 2018.Ringing was only the beginning of the day. Hurst also cleaned buildings, repaired gates, conducted wildlife surveys and helped manage habitats. About 150 bird species have been recorded on the island, including Manx shearwaters, razorbills and shags, according to Hurst's 2024 interview. Wardens also monitor seals, survey butterflies, record dragonflies and damselflies, and trap moths for identification. The surrounding waters form the Calf of Man and Wart Bank Marine Nature Reserve. Hurst said she had seen around 40 people on the island at once during the open season.When the boat does not comeBad weather can prevent boats from reaching the Calf, delaying food and other supplies and leaving wardens unable to leave by their usual route. Hurst said the team sometimes waited two to three weeks for a boat, so the wardens kept tinned food and emergency rations in reserve. In a genuine emergency, they could contact the Coastguard for helicopter evacuation. Boat travel is therefore the normal route to and from the island, but it is not the only possible means of emergency evacuation.A Manx Wildlife Trust job description for an assistant bird warden states that the seasonal placement runs from early March to early November. Leave must be arranged so that at least two wardens remain on the Calf at all times, allowing the observatory and estate work to continue.Hurst described her 2022 experience as one of the best periods of her life and returned in 2024 as a paid estate warden. Press reports placed the pay for the later seasonal post at around £19,000. Her advice to anyone considering similar conservation work is to research the role carefully, prepare for basic living conditions and be ready to adapt when weather delays supplies and ordinary shopping trips are not possible.You use AI every day. articles.title: By 2009, seeking a low-impact countryside life in Wales, Simon Dale built a straw-insulated woodland “Hobbit house” with his family in three months for £3,000
articles.summary: Discover how Simon Dale and his family built an eco-friendly \"Hobbit house\" in Wales for just £3,000 using sustainable materials and techniques. Learn about the construction process, insulation effectiveness of straw, and the development of the Lammas ecovillage.
articles.body: Many families cannot afford a country home, and renting can mean decades of payments with little to show for it. In response, some people raise doubts about the entire construction process. Rather than placing an order for bricks and cement, they question what a house might look like if it were built on nearby land, cost very little, and left virtually no environmental damage.Simon Dale approached the problem by building a woodland home in west Wales that resembles a house from Tolkien's Shire. With help from his father-in-law, friends and passersby, he used straw bales for insulation and local or reclaimed materials to reduce the need for new building supplies. By 2009, Dale was also involved in the Lammas ecovillage in Pembrokeshire, which received planning permission on appeal that year.Dale's own account says the family moved in four months after work began. He estimated that the project had taken 1,000 to 1,500 hours of labour and cost about £3,000 at that stage, excluding labour. The fun part about the project is the open-endedness of the numbers. The £3,000 number doesn’t cover everything, and a look at how the house was built, whether straw really insulates and how one hillside home evolved into a town illustrates what it does cover.Building the woodland homeEarth is the starting point of the design. Dale built into a hillside to provide shelter and reduce the house's visual impact. He used stone and mud from the excavation in the retaining walls and foundations, and made the frame from oak thinnings from nearby woodland. Reclaimed wood supplied the floors and fittings. A waterproof plastic sheet lies beneath the mud and turf roof. The house therefore combines natural and reclaimed materials with a synthetic waterproof layer. Inside, lime plaster provides a breathable finish and requires less energy to produce than cement.Most of the work was done with simple tools. Dale described using a chainsaw, a hammer and a one-inch chisel, with his father-in-law and visiting friends doing much of the heavy lifting. He put the cost at roughly £60 per square metre, not counting labour. A wood burner heats the house, and a solar panel provides power. Reports on the project also describe a fridge cooled by underground airflow and a composting toilet.The purpose for developing this manner was as much lifestyle as it was architectural. Dale describes how the house allowed his family to live close to nature, carrying out sustainable woodland management and creating a forest garden, tasks that would have been impossible with a regular rent or mortgage to pay.Does straw really insulate?Straw often raises questions, so it is worth looking at what the research says. A 2019 laboratory study published in Sustainability measured average thermal conductivity of 0.0573 watts per metre kelvin for dry wheat straw at a density of roughly 80 kilograms per cubic metre. For comparison, the study measured 0.041 for expanded polystyrene. The authors suggested increasing the straw figure by about 20%, to roughly 0.07, to account for moisture and ageing in actual buildings.In the study's comparison, the straw wall had a U value of 0.281 with a thickness of 20 centimetres, close to the Italian standard limit of 0.29. The polystyrene wall achieved 0.181. This 20 centimetre comparison should not be treated as representative of typical straw bale construction, where walls are usually much thicker, around 450 to 500 millimetres. The report states that such walls often achieve U values between 0.13 and 0.19. The straw walls also blocked sound more effectively than the polystyrene walls, although their thermal mass may not prevent overheating during hot, sunny weather.Moisture is the real risk. The paper cites work showing that straw stays sound below 20 per cent moisture content and begins to decompose above 30%, so breathable finishes matter. That is exactly the role of Dale’s lime plaster. The embodied energy of straw is also low. One estimate cited in the study puts it at about 28 megajoules per square metre of wall, against 488 for fired bricks and 169 for concrete blocks.From one house to a community projectDale's house was not the only low-impact project in the area. The Lammas ecovillage went through a lengthy planning process before receiving permission on appeal in 2009. Lowimpact.org has described the site as having nine households, about 15 structures and thousands of planted trees. These are approximate figures describing a collection of smallholdings, rather than a large town.A wider policy for similar projects followed. Wales introduced the One Planet Development policy through Technical Advice Note 6 in July 2010. Under the guidance, developments must demonstrate within five years that residents can meet their basic needs through land-based activities. Established developments are expected to achieve an ecological footprint of 2.4 global hectares per person, with a clear path towards 1.88. The policy also calls for buildings with zero-carbon construction and use. Lammas estimates that the land-based income requirement works out at about £3,000 per adult each year.The model still demands considerable effort. Residents must build and maintain their homes, meet basic needs through land-based activities and raise their families. One Lammas resident described the demands as exhausting and said the lifestyle would not suit everyone. Dale's estimate of £3,000 represented the amount spent at that stage, excluding labour. It should not be treated as the total cost of a typical home, since land, planning, infrastructure and unpaid work can add substantially to the effort and expense. Dale's project depended on local and reclaimed materials and help from family, friends and passersby. It is an example of one family's self-built home, not a universal £3,000 housing model.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Hannah Jeter grew up on a three-mile-wide Caribbean island, played on the national tennis circuit and was discovered as a model at 14
articles.summary: Hannah Jeter's journey to becoming a recognised model began far from the fashion capitals of the world.
articles.body: Hannah Jeter's journey to becoming a recognised model began far from the fashion capitals of the world. Raised on St Thomas in the US Virgin Islands, she spent her childhood playing competitive tennis and pursuing ambitions that had little to do with the modelling industry. Her life took a different direction when she was discovered at the age of 14, opening the door to international assignments and a career in fashion. Before becoming widely known as the wife of former New York Yankees star Derek Jeter, she had already built a life shaped by sport, travel and independence.How did Hannah Jeter's Caribbean childhood shape her early ambitionsHannah Jeter, born Hannah Bethany Davis on 5 May 1990, grew up on St Thomas, an island in the Caribbean that measures approximately 3 miles across. According to The Players' Tribune, her upbringing was a world away from the baseball culture that would later become part of her life through her relationship with Derek Jeter.Hannah explained that baseball was not a major part of life where she grew up. The island did not have professional teams for residents to follow, and she had little reason to pay attention to American baseball stars.Instead, sport played a different role in her childhood. Tennis became a central part of her life, giving her a goal to work towards before the modelling industry entered the picture.According to the profile on Nicki Swift, she was the youngest of three children and shared a particularly close bond with her older brother, Conn Davis Jr. She admired him and often wanted to do the same things he did. Her childhood style reflected that preference, as she gravitated towards cargo trousers and trainers rather than a traditionally feminine look.These early experiences helped shape a personality that was comfortable with sport and competition, long before she became associated with fashion and celebrity life.Tennis gave her a competitive start before modellingTennis was more than a childhood pastime for Hannah. She competed on the Caribbean tennis circuit and was involved in the sport at a serious level. According to Nicki Swift, she was discovered by a local scout while playing on the circuit.The opportunity came at a time when she was focused on developing her sporting abilities. Modelling was not initially the career she had set out to pursue. Instead, it presented a possible way to support her ambitions on the tennis court.Hannah reflected on how quickly she had grown up after beginning work as a model at 14. She travelled internationally for assignments and gradually developed a career of her own.The experience also meant spending time away from home while managing professional commitments at a young age. She later explained that travelling from job to job had pushed her towards adulthood earlier than she might otherwise have expected.Her discovery at 14 opened the door to an international careerHannah's move into modelling began when she was still a teenager. IMDb's biography records that she was discovered at the beach at the age of 14. The modelling industry offered an opportunity to earn money while continuing to pursue her sporting ambitions. Nicki Swift reported how modelling initially seemed like a practical way to help pay for tennis lessons and equipment.What began as a means of supporting her sporting interests gradually became a career in its own right. As her assignments increased, she faced the challenge of balancing two demanding pursuits. Travelling for modelling work made it harder to maintain the same level of training she had previously managed. Eventually, her professional direction shifted towards fashion.Her early start also meant that she experienced considerable independence while still young. She had travelled around the world and established her own career before meeting Derek Jeter.That experience became an important part of how she understood their relationship. Both had developed their own lives and ambitions before they met, rather than beginning their adult journeys together.Meeting Derek Jeter brought a different kind of public attentionHannah met Derek Jeter through a mutual friend while having dinner with her mother in New York. As reported in The Players' Tribune, she recalled that she did not fully understand his standing in American baseball when they were introduced.She knew his name but had not followed his career closely. She initially thought he was a pitcher rather than a shortstop. The couple began dating in 2012, according to Nicki Swift. Their relationship developed during the baseball off-season, which gave them an opportunity to spend time together away from the constant attention surrounding Derek's professional career.She wanted to know him as a person rather than through information available online or his public reputation. Their early relationship allowed her to form her own impression of him.That changed when she attended a New York Yankees game at Yankee Stadium. Seeing the crowd's reaction helped her understand the scale of his popularity and the emotional connection fans had developed with him over two decades.Paparazzi sometimes followed the couple, and people interrupted them during meals. Staying at home became one way to protect their privacy.Her modelling career continued alongside changes in her personal lifeHannah's relationship with Derek developed while both were managing demanding careers. She gradually came to appreciate how much baseball meant to him, particularly as his playing career approached its end.During his final season with the Yankees in 2014, she travelled to some of his games and cancelled professional assignments to be present. She admitted that understanding the full significance of his career took time, but his final game at Yankee Stadium helped her appreciate the connection between the player and his supporters.Nicki Swift reported that the couple married in California in 2016. Hannah later discussed their hopes of raising children who could enjoy a relatively normal life despite their father's fame.
